findings.title: A designed route around the king's law
findings.claim: The arranged search turns the brothers' own stated sanction into a route by which custody can occur even though the king's customary order would not itself authorize it.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the indirect arrangement in كِدْ, the taking of the brother in يَأْخُذَ, the established order named by دِينِ, and the public authority named by مَلِكِ. Their contact changes the search from a bare discovery of a cup into a designed transfer of custody through a different jurisdictional route; the exact wider connections at 7:183 and 86:15 keep deliberate counter-planning in view, while 109:6 supplies the governing-order sense of din.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the search order matters: it produces the condition that lets the brothers' own rule do work the royal rule cannot do.
findings.containment: This does not establish a formal legal theory beyond the ayah, endorse every stratagem, or collapse the possible meanings of the king's din into one model; it keeps the local custody and jurisdictional contrast intact.

epistemic.reason: The finding is supported by the citable trusted publication and accepted focus branches; wider connection rows add exact target Arabic as qualified relational evidence rather than an independent lexical analysis.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The following taking, the king's din, the king's authority, and the wider exact-Arabic planning parallels supply the separate legal and procedural conditions.
branch_activations.activation: The word for arrangement meets the focus's taking and jurisdictional terms, so the plan is read as the mechanism that makes custody possible through an available route.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The stratagem is an operative legal detour, not decorative concealment.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch is not generalized to every secret plan and is not treated as an automatic moral verdict.

findings.title: Elevation with a ceiling above it
findings.claim: The successful arrangement raises a person through degrees while the closing knowledge hierarchy prevents that elevation from becoming absolute mastery.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries staged movement in دَرَجَاتٍ, active elevation in نَرْفَعُ, comparative superiority in فَوْقَ, and knowing in عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ. The degree and elevation carriers contact the higher-than relation and the paired knowledge terms; exact wider Arabic at 6:83, 58:11, 20:114, and 17:85 reinforces bestowed elevation and the limit placed on every human knower. The result is a ladder whose next rung remains above each knower, including the strategist who succeeds.
findings.reader_payoff: The final maxim becomes part of the episode's action: success marks a real rise, and the same sentence keeps that rise from turning into omniscience.
findings.containment: This does not rank the people in the story by a final human scale, reduce elevation to social status, or make the wider parallels identical to the focus; the qualified knowledge branch keeps the claim bounded to the stated hierarchy.

epistemic.reason: The trusted publication and exact focus carriers support the relation, while the knowledge branch is packet-qualified and the connection rows lack target morphology, so the synthesis remains qualified.

findings.title: The order makes the reveal look found
findings.claim: Beginning with the others and placing the brother's vessel later makes the final extraction appear to arise from an ordered search, so sequence itself manages suspicion.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb بَدَأَ carries the opening action and قَبْلَ marks the others' vessels as prior to the brother's vessel. Their contact with the later extraction changes the scene from an undifferentiated search into a staged disclosure whose public appearance is procedural.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the order of inspection is part of what makes the cup's discovery credible within the scene.
findings.containment: This preserves the ayah's stated search and does not claim that every procedural order is deceptive, that Yusuf's intent is exhausted by suspicion-management, or that the unresolved alternate b-d-ء mapping is established.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk support is legacy_unbound and one cited root mapping is unresolved; the retained core uses the supplied nominated opening branch and accepted before-order branch only.

findings.title: The vessels hold objects and expectations
findings.claim: The repeated vessels remain physical containers while also giving the search a secondary image of holding information and managing what observers expect to see.
findings.mechanism: The three supplied وِعَآء occurrences carry the accepted container branch, while the same root's holding-in-memory branch is activated by the ordered search and by the exact wider retaining-ear connection at 69:12. The direct container parallel at 70:18 joins collecting with putting into a vessel, so the final extraction changes the repeated vessel from mere scenery into the material place where both an object and an expectation have been held.
findings.reader_payoff: The cup scene becomes legible as a controlled release: something is taken from a vessel, and an expectation formed around the vessels is released or reversed with it.
findings.containment: The inner-holding image is a qualified contextual resonance, not a replacement for the literal vessels, not a claim about hidden mental states for every observer, and not an activation of the packet's other w-y-ʿ branches.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk source is legacy_unbound; the two retained branches are accepted, and the wider connections provide exact target Arabic but no target morphology.
